name: CT-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Rosa DeLauro is a long-serving incumbent in a district with an 8-point Democratic lean
DeLauro has raised over $1.1 million versus about $15,000 for Republican Chris Lancia
Prediction markets price DeLauro at roughly 95% to win
No public polling of the general election, but fundamentals point strongly Democratic
model.rationale: DeLauro combines incumbency, a Democratic-leaning district, and an overwhelming fundraising advantage against a barely funded challenger, and markets price her near-certain to win. With no contrary polling or ratings evidence, the fundamentals-based margin of about 20 points stands.
model.watch: A surprise national Republican wave or an unexpectedly well-funded challenger effort could narrow the margin, though an upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rosa DeLauro, one of the House's longest-serving members, seeks another term in a Connecticut district that leans Democratic by about eight points. She enters the general election after easily securing renomination, with roughly $350,000 on hand and more than $1.1 million raised, supplemented by modest outside support.

Republican Chris Lancia has raised only about $15,000, leaving him with little capacity to communicate with voters, and an independent candidate also appears on the ballot. No public polls cover the race, but prediction markets give DeLauro about a 95% chance of winning. The combination of incumbency, district lean, and financial dominance makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with an expected margin near 20 points.
